titulo: Tech Rout and US Midterm Shift Roil Global Markets
resumo: November brought heightened volatility to financial markets as political realignments collided with reassessments of artificial intelligence expenditure. The **US midterm elections delivered a Democratic sweep** of Congress, triggering swift sector rotations and sudden policy uncertainty over data centre developments. Technology shares endured severe turbulence, dragging the Nasdaq Composite down 4.4% month to date to 24315. In response, **the VIX volatility index jumped 45.1%** to 28.18 as investors sought safe havens in government paper. Meanwhile, Brent crude retreated 10.9% to $107.03 a barrel, offering temporary energy cost respite against broader inflationary pressures.

sumup.frase: Political upheaval and technology doubts ignited **surging volatility** across asset classes.
sumup.porque: Tech stock turbulence and political shifts pushed the VIX volatility gauge sharply higher.

drivers.texto: Democrats flipped control of both the House and Senate in the US midterms. Equities staged an initial broad relief rally before policy anxieties regarding technology regulations and data centre moratoriums sparked sharp declines. Following the shift, the S&P 500 fell 3% month to date to 7353.73.

Scrutiny over substantial capital expenditure and computing costs triggered a severe tech sell-off, with the Nasdaq Composite dropping 4.4% month to date to 24315. Investors grew wary of commitments such as Anthropic reporting $895.4 billion in purchase commitments alongside $17 billion in Q3 revenue. Volatility jumped markedly, with the Cboe VIX surging 45.1% to 28.18.

Brent crude slid 10.9% month to date to $107.03 a barrel as optimism grew over possible US-Iran peace talks. The drop provided brief relief to transport and industrial firms facing high fuel costs. Despite this monthly decline, oil prices remained up 74.5% year to date.

The Bank of England raised its key interest rate to 4%, representing its first increase in over three years. The tightening moved borrowing costs higher for UK consumers and businesses amid ongoing cost-of-living challenges. In Europe, the European Central Bank held its deposit rate steady at 2.5%.

The US economy added 165,000 jobs in October, surpassing market expectations and demonstrating ongoing labour resilience. The sturdy labour report briefly halted a haven rally in sovereign debt. Benchmark US 10-year Treasury yields stood at 4.9%, down 4 basis points this month.

themes.texto: Markets began sharply re-evaluating the economics of artificial intelligence infrastructure and chip demand. Mega deals such as Marvell's acquisition of Lumentum occurred alongside mounting operational costs and extended computing bills across developers. Investor unease wiped trillions in market value from tech shares, sending the Nasdaq Composite down 4.4% to 24315. Consequently, corporate budgets and power grid limits are replacing unbridled optimism as primary market drivers.

The Democratic sweep of both houses of Congress altered sector outlooks overnight. Calls for national data centre moratoriums and probes into energy and corporate relationships quickly followed the election. While renewable energy and hospital stocks saw initial buying interest, broader equities suffered as policy uncertainty mounted. The S&P 500 fell 3% to 7353.73, while corporate credit spreads widened slightly by 4 basis points to 3.48.

themes.titulo: Persistent global inflation and divergent policies
themes.texto: Euro area inflation stood at 4% in October, while Portugal recorded a 3.9% annual rate and a 12-month average of 2.9%. Central bank paths diverged as the Bank of England raised rates to 4% whilst the ECB kept its deposit rate at 2.5%. With Portuguese 10-year sovereign bond yields averaging 3.85% and the 12-month Euribor at 3.239%, persistent inflation continues to prevent aggressive monetary easing across Europe.

questoes.q: Can tech firms justify immense capital spending on AI infrastructure?
questoes.porque: Computing bills and power infrastructure are eroding margins across major software and semiconductor enterprises. A pullback in tech investment could drag down broader global equity benchmarks.
questoes.sinais: Upcoming quarterly earnings reports and updated cloud infrastructure capital expenditure budgets.

questoes.q: Will legislative gridlock impede US fiscal and regulatory agendas?
questoes.porque: A divided government facing a lame-duck administration creates friction over debt ceilings and regulatory reviews. This can elevate sovereign risk premiums and bond market volatility.
questoes.sinais: Congressional debates regarding proposed national data centre moratoriums and the US debt limit.

questoes.q: Will European inflation cool sufficiently to allow ECB rate cuts?
questoes.porque: Euro area inflation of 4% remains elevated, keeping borrowing costs high for businesses and homeowners. In Portugal, new mortgage rates stand at 3.06% against term deposit rates of 1.83%.
questoes.sinais: Preliminary flash HICP inflation figures for November across the euro area.

momentos.facto: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance resumed withdrawals after suffering a record $6.3 billion cyber hack.
Brent crude fell 10.9% month to date to $107.03 a barrel on hopes of US-Iran diplomatic talks.
Democrats swept the US midterm elections, winning majorities in both the Senate and the House of Representatives.
The Bank of England raised its benchmark interest rate to 4%, marking its first hike in three years.
The Cboe VIX volatility index jumped 45.1% to 28.18 as global tech stocks plunged over AI spending fears.
US non-farm payrolls showed the economy added 165,000 jobs in October, beating analyst expectations.

classes.leitura: Global equity markets fell sharply as the S&P 500 declined 3% and the Nasdaq sank 4.4% amid a heavy tech and data centre sell-off.
Sovereign debt saw safe-haven bids, pushing US 10-year yields down 4 basis points to 4.9% and euro area 10-year AAA yields down 7 basis points to 3.2938%.
Brent crude slid 10.9% to $107.03 a barrel on US-Iran dialogue prospects, whilst industrial copper prices softened.
The euro held relatively steady against the US dollar, with the EUR/USD exchange rate dipping 0.1% month to date to 1.1165.
US high-yield credit spreads widened by 4 basis points to 3.48 as risk sentiment deteriorated following the tech sector pullback.

vigiar: Legislative proposals from the incoming Democratic US congressional majority regarding artificial intelligence regulations and data centre moratoriums.
Euro area and Portuguese inflation updates to assess whether the ECB will keep its deposit rate at 2.5%.
Developments in diplomatic talks between the US and Iran influencing global crude oil supply and prices.
Further capital expenditure announcements and IPO developments among major artificial intelligence hardware and model developers.
